title: Grateful Dead Live at Baltimore Civic Center on 1972-09-17
source: Audience (taper Cary Wolfson) > Cass > DAT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Good 1972 audience tape capturing a high‑energy show with standout Bird Song, He's Gone > Other One, and Jerry’s killer Sing Me Back Home solo
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience (AUD) capture that sounds surprisingly clear for its era, despite some vocal inconsistencies, occasional muffled moments and persistent tambourine chatter. Musically the show shines – Bird Song, He's Gone into a monster Other One, Sugar Magnolia, Playing in the Band, Half‑Step and a soaring Sing Me Back Home solo make it a fan favorite. Overall the performance is high‑energy and the tape is a worthwhile addition for any 1972 collector.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (≈90%) give 4–5 stars, praising both the musical performance and the surprisingly good AUD sound; only a few note minor flaws, yielding an overall high rating with strong consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Decent clarity for a 1972 AUD; vocals hit‑or‑miss, occasional muffled Truckin' due to mic cap, noticeable tambourine but overall listenable and better than many contemporary audience tapes.

standout_songs: He's Gone > Other One > Sing Me Back Home
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set solid with classic numbers; second set flows seamlessly through He's Gone into a monster Other One and a soaring Sing Me Back Home, highlighted by Jerry’s solo. The show maintains momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers rave about his tone and a 'cowboy' solo on Sing Me Back Home; also praised for ripping Sugar Magnolia (4:58‑6:03).
band_member_comments.Phil: One reviewer notes an odd, synth‑like bass sound at ~30:12 in The Other One, calling it uniquely Phil.
